name: shellbox

modes.label: On-demand (Firecracker VM, default)
modes.note: Running: $0.02/h per x1 slot, billed per minute. Parked (stopped) boxes: $0.50/month per x1 slot, covering the memory snapshot + disk (encoded as storage.snapshot_gib_month = $0.50 / 50 GB x1 disk = $0.01/GiB-month). Default backend Firecracker (fast snapshots); Cloud Hypervisor boxes (--ch, nested virt) are the separate 'cloud-hypervisor' mode at the same slot rates. Do not multiply running price by CPU utilization.

modes.label: Cloud Hypervisor VM (--ch, nested virtualization)
modes.note: Same slot rates as the Firecracker default ('$0.02/hr per x1 slot, billed per minute' for both backends); created with `ssh shellbox.dev create mybox --ch`; /dev/kvm available inside.

plans.name: Prepaid
plans.note: 16 running slots and 64 total slots per account; each box counts as its size in slots (x1 = 2 vCPU). So 16 x1, 8 x2 (4 vCPU/8 GB) or 2 x8 boxes can run at once: concurrency 16 is the x1 upper bound; max_total_vcpu 32 (= 16 slots x 2 vCPU) is the real cap (engine support requested). $10 minimum prepaid top-up; boxes stop below $5 balance and are deleted at $0.

caveats: Public list price per x1 slot. Running and parked are mutually exclusive time states. SSH key identifies account; prepaid $10 minimum top-up. Sizes scale linearly x1 to x8.

16 running slots and 64 total slots per account; a box counts as its size in slots, so a 4 vCPU/8 GB (x2) box allows 8 concurrent. Encoded as plan concurrency 16 (x1 bound) + max_total_vcpu 32; the engine does not yet enforce slot-weighted quota (see research/verify/engine-requests.md).

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

Parked fee $0.50/x1 slot-month is per slot, not per GiB; snapshot_gib_month 0.01 = $0.50 / 50 GB assumes the retained state equals the box disk size. Parked storage is otherwise free ("memory snapshots ... on NVMe, rootfs images ... on HDDs"). No desktop/GUI/browser image is documented (desktop/browser/computer_use=false). (shellbox.dev, 2026-09-28)

fleet.verification: Account automatically identified by SSH-key fingerprint (no email/password signup). Prepaid $10 minimum via Paddle; no card stored by Shellbox.
fleet.tiers: 16 running x1-equivalent slots and 64 total slots/user; an xN box uses N slots. No documented paid quota ladder.
fleet.notes: 16-machine upper bound applies ONLY to smallest x1 (2 vCPU/4 GB); derived vCPU pool 16×2=32. A 4 vCPU/8 GB box consumes 2 slots, permitting only 8 running. 10 such machines or 50/300/1,000 any-size exceed defaults; raise procedure and timing unpublished.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: After the last SSH session disconnects, wait 120 seconds, then pause. Snapshot saves processes, shell history, and TCP state; restored on next connect.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: last SSH session disconnects (+120 s grace), idle timeout in wakeup mode, end of a cron run window, or balance < $5. Memory included (Firecracker/CH memory snapshot on NVMe); restored transparently on next SSH/HTTP connect (~3 s claimed, blog says under a second).

snapshot_on_demand.note: `ssh shellbox.dev stop <name>` snapshots (memory + disk) at any time; `duplicate <src> <new>` forks a box incl. its memory snapshot via btrfs reflink (FAQ: 'duplicate a stopped box as a point-in-time copy'). No named snapshot list / rollback-in-place; each copy is a whole box (billed as a parked slot).

harness_api.quote: Start a tmux or zellij session, launch your agent, and disconnect:
harness_api.note: The FAQ tells you to run Claude Code/Codex yourself inside the box over SSH; the complete command reference (help --json) has no agent/harness commands.

ingress_rules.quote: HTTP requests to this URL are proxied to port 80 on your box.
ingress_rules.note: Every box gets a public HTTPS URL (port 80 only) plus a stable public IPv6 reachable for ssh/mosh/raw TCP-UDP while running. No auth, private-URL, IP allowlist or port-selection controls documented; custom domains only add hostnames. The fixed port-80 routing is the only provider-side restriction on the HTTPS path.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker (default) or Cloud Hypervisor microVMs, 'each with its own kernel and disk', login as root. Given the directly public IPv6, an in-guest firewall is the only way to filter inbound. Not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: Your private key never leaves your machine.
secret_proxy.note: No secret store or credential proxy. The docs recommend SSH agent forwarding for git (key stays on the client, but a live agent socket is exposed in the box while connected) or pasting tokens / copying private keys into the box.

volume_attach.quote: Size is set at creation and cannot be changed — delete and recreate to resize.
volume_attach.note: Disk is fixed by size multiplier (50 GB per x1, up to 400 GB at x8); no volume commands in the command reference.

volume_shared.note: No shared/network filesystem or multi-box volume mount is documented; each box's disk is fixed at creation ('Size is set at creation and cannot be changed — delete and recreate to resize') and duplicate only clones a box (reflink copy), it doesn't share a live volume across boxes.

anti_bot.quote: Firecracker microVM ... You SSH into a VM and run whatever processes you want inside it.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (a plain SSH-accessible Linux microVM, not a browser/scraping product; no browser, no stealth/fingerprinting features documented anywhere on the site)

captcha_solving.quote: Firecracker microVM ... You SSH into a VM and run whatever processes you want inside it.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no browser or CAPTCHA-related feature is documented; this is a general-purpose SSH VM, not a scraping/automation product)

egress_ip_type.quote: Every new box gets a stable public IPv6 address derived from the box's network identity.
egress_ip_type.note: Each box has its own dedicated, stable public IPv6 (no shared/NATed pool documented); servers run on Hetzner infra in Helsinki, Finland, i.e. datacenter IP space. No public IPv4 is offered.

fork_running.note: The `duplicate` command's own JSON help text and FAQ ("duplicate a stopped box as a point-in-time copy") both specify the source box must be stopped; no running-clone path is documented.

live_resize.quote: Size is set at creation and cannot be changed — delete and recreate to resize.

agent_harnesses.quote: Start a tmux or zellij session, launch your agent, and disconnect: ... root@mybox:~# claude # or your agent of choice
agent_harnesses.note: Coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) are things you install and run yourself over SSH inside a stock Ubuntu box; none are preinstalled or offered as a selectable template.

own_agent_api.quote: The full API covers box lifecycle (create, list, show, duplicate, rename, stop, delete), modes (keepalive, wakeup, cron), OCI images ... billing ... and key management.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The entire documented API/CLI surface is VM lifecycle management; there is no browser/computer-use/research agent product of Shellbox's own.

mcp_server.quote: The full API covers box lifecycle (create, list, show, duplicate, rename, stop, delete), modes (keepalive, wakeup, cron), OCI images ... billing ... and key management.
mcp_server.note: No MCP server is mentioned anywhere on the site; the only documented control surfaces are the SSH-based CLI/JSON API.

lang_python.note: Stock boxes ship Ubuntu 24.04 LTS; the FAQ uses `python3` directly as a working example with no install step shown, implying it is present out of the box.

public_ipv4.quote: Do boxes have public IPv6? Yes. Every new box gets a stable public IPv6 address...
public_ipv4.note: The FAQ documents public IPv6 only; IPv4 is never mentioned anywhere on the site.

egress_allowlist.quote: Firecracker microVM ... You SSH into a VM and run whatever processes you want inside it.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No allow/deny-list, no-internet mode, or security-group egress feature is documented; the product is a bare root VM with full outbound access.

egress_http_rules.quote: Firecracker microVM ... You SSH into a VM and run whatever processes you want inside it.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No HTTP method/path-level egress control is documented anywhere on the site.

static_egress_ip.quote: Every new box gets a stable public IPv6 address derived from the box's network identity.
static_egress_ip.note: Each box keeps one dedicated, stable IPv6 address for its lifetime (shown via `show`/`list`); not explicitly labeled 'egress IP' but it is the box's only network identity, so outbound traffic is not NATed through a shared/rotating pool.

gpu.quote: Base box (x1): 2 vCPUs, 4GB RAM, 50GB SSD. Sizes scale up to x8 (16 vCPUs, 32GB RAM, 400GB SSD).
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. All documented sizes (x1-x8) are CPU/RAM/disk only; no GPU option is mentioned anywhere.

windows.quote: Stock boxes ship with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Docker pre-installed.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. The product is Firecracker/Cloud Hypervisor Linux microVMs; no Windows image or OS option is documented.

macos.quote: Stock boxes ship with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Docker pre-installed.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Firecracker/Cloud Hypervisor cannot run macOS guests, and no macOS option is documented.

self_host.quote: Currently in Europe (Helsinki, Finland). A US region is planned...
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Shellbox is offered only as a hosted SaaS on its own infrastructure; no self-hosted/on-prem distribution is documented.

byoc.quote: Currently in Europe (Helsinki, Finland). A US region is planned...
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No option to deploy Shellbox into a customer's own cloud account is documented.

open_source.note: The only public GitHub repo linked from the site is an issue tracker (shellbox.issues), not the product's source code; no license or source repo for the actual service is published.

soc2.quote: No signup, no email, no password required. ... Prepaid $10 minimum top-up via Paddle.
soc2.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a single self-serve prepaid plan for individual developers with no enterprise/compliance page; no SOC 2 attestation is mentioned anywhere.

hipaa.quote: No signup, no email, no password required. ... Prepaid $10 minimum top-up via Paddle.
hipaa.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No BAA/HIPAA-eligibility is mentioned; the product targets individual developers via anonymous SSH-key accounts.

sso.quote: No signup, no email, no password required. The first time you connect, your account is created automatically from your SSH key fingerprint.
sso.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Authentication is SSH-key-fingerprint-based with no accounts/org concept; no SAML/OIDC SSO is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: Where are the servers located? Currently in Europe (Helsinki, Finland). A US region is planned...
eu_data_residency.note: All boxes currently run in the EU (Finland); this is the only available region today.

max_session_h.quote: If you want a box to keep running after disconnect (e.g. for a background job), toggle keepalive: ssh shellbox.dev keepalive <name>
max_session_h.note: With keepalive enabled a box runs indefinitely until explicitly stopped; no maximum session duration is documented.

desktop.quote: shellbox turns a Docker/OCI image into the root filesystem of a normal microVM. ... You SSH into a VM and run whatever processes you want inside it.
desktop.note: Shellbox is an SSH-only Firecracker/Cloud-Hypervisor microVM box; the full FAQ, resource-limits, and command-reference sections never mention VNC/RDP/desktop streaming or a GUI image. Access is exclusively via SSH (and SFTP/port-forwarding over SSH).

browser.quote: Configure your browser or tools to use localhost:1080 as a SOCKS5 proxy.
browser.note: The only 'browser' references on the page are about using the user's own local browser/SOCKS proxy to reach a box's ports; no managed/hosted browser is offered or documented anywhere on the page.

computer_use.quote: Start a tmux or zellij session, launch your agent, and disconnect
computer_use.note: The FAQ's agent-workflow guidance is entirely SSH/CLI-based (tmux, agent binaries run manually); there is no screenshot+click computer-use API or product surface documented anywhere on the page.

arm64.quote: Current OCI support focuses on: Public images (no private registries yet) linux/amd64 architecture
arm64.note: Explicit OCI image support statement plus the API's `image status` example both show amd64 ('Architecture: amd64'); no arm64/aarch64 offering is mentioned anywhere on the page.
